issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, Interval Operators / Intersect: intersect returns the overlapping portion of both intervals and returns null when the arguments do not overlap.
issues.evidence: .temp/qa/cql16_skeptic_probe.py: Interval[1, 5) intersect Interval[5, 7] should be null because the first interval excludes 5. Forced Python and native-loaded return {"low":"5","high":"5","lowClosed":true,"highClosed":true}; no-Python C++ returns null. The same bad value is produced by translated CQL IntersectOpenDisjoint.

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, Interval Operators / Overlaps: overlaps before/after are overlap plus boundary-order predicates using Start/End semantics; date/time precision comparisons can be unknown and incompatible Quantity comparisons propagate null.
issues.evidence: .temp/qa/cql16_skeptic_probe.py: partial temporal cases such as Interval[@2014, @2014] overlaps before Interval[@2014-06-01, @2014-06-02] return false on all three surfaces instead of null. Incompatible Quantity cases return false in forced Python/native-loaded and null in no-Python C++, causing both wrong semantics and parity divergence. Translated CQL reproduces the same false/null mismatch.
